verdict.justification: Both drafts correctly apply the approved r2 requirement for Finance, Program Manager and Purchase approval, rather than treating the later Purchase-only proposal as authoritative. B is the stronger platform blueprint because its change-routing table explicitly identifies TRSO signatories, commercial treatment and price-change approvers for every change class. It also makes the no-cost route more defensible by requiring supplier confirmation of a “zero delta” and reclassification if a price claim emerges, whereas A mainly specifies recording and notification. B provides more actionable gate controls, including mandatory rejection comments and the explicit safeguard that “Escalation never auto-approves”; A leaves its separate “G3: Commercial clearance” without clearly named signatories. B’s modular model is also more commercially complete, explicitly separating conversion, overheads and one-time costs and adding cumulative cost-delta monitoring. Its proceed-at-risk concept warrants careful review, but it is clearly labeled a proposal requiring confirmation, not an existing authority or implemented action.

decisive_issues.issue: The separate commercial-clearance gate does not clearly specify its required approvers.
The no-cost change route lacks the explicit supplier zero-delta confirmation and reclassification control supplied by B.
